# Chignolin AlphaFold prediction

This experiment tested AlphaFold2 on the ten-residue chignolin sequence as a small folding-model case.

## Question

Can AlphaFold2 produce a useful structure prediction for the small foldable peptide chignolin (`GYDPETGTWG`)?

## Configuration

- Input: `GYDPETGTWG` (ten residues), supplied as `experiments/chignolin-prediction/chignolin.fasta`.
- Software: ColabFold 1.6.2, AlphaFold2 pTM models, CPU backend.
- MSA: `single_sequence`, with `max_msa=1:1`; no evolutionary homologues were supplied.
- Five models, seed 0, three recycling iterations.
- Results: [experiment results directory](../experiments/chignolin-prediction/results).

## Result

The run completed and produced five ranked PDB structures. The best-ranked model was AlphaFold2 pTM model 1.

| Output | Best-ranked value |
|---|---:|
| Mean pLDDT (mean of 10 residue scores) | 93.4 |
| pTM | 0.06 |
| Maximum predicted aligned error | 5.35 Å |

The high local pLDDT and very low pTM are the measured outputs of this run, not a claim that the peptide was correctly folded. The result indicates confident local geometry but poor global-fold confidence under this single-sequence configuration. The pTM score is especially relevant because chignolin is a short peptide with no informative MSA in this setup. This result supports the caution in [AlphaFold limitations and inference](AlphaFold-Limitations-and-Inference) that accuracy is conditional on input information and that AlphaFold predicts a static structure rather than a folding trajectory.

## Images

The following images are stored with this wiki page.

![Illustrative unfolded and folded chignolin](images/Chignolin-AlphaFold/chignolin-before-after.png)

The before/after image is an explanatory illustration generated for this experiment. It is not a rendering of the predicted PDB and does not represent a measured trajectory.

![Per-residue pLDDT confidence](images/Chignolin-AlphaFold/chignolin-plddt.png)

![Predicted aligned error](images/Chignolin-AlphaFold/chignolin-pae.png)

## Interpretation and limits

This was a structure-prediction check, not a folding simulation. It does not estimate folded-state populations, transition rates, or a free-energy surface. The single-sequence MSA removes the evolutionary signal that AlphaFold normally exploits, and the capped Ace–chignolin–Nme molecule was not modeled: the input was the ten-residue sequence alone. Absence of caps means this output should not be treated as a prediction for the capped experimental molecule.

The AlphaFold paper reports pLDDT as a per-residue accuracy estimate and pTM as a global superposition estimate; neither is an experimental measurement for this peptide. A meaningful folding study would require an explicit capped molecular model and molecular-dynamics or enhanced-sampling trajectories, with validation against a reference structure or free-energy landscape.

## Reproducibility

The FASTA, configuration, logs, PDB files, score JSON files and confidence plots are in [the experiment results directory](../experiments/chignolin-prediction/results). The top model is [the rank-001 PDB](../experiments/chignolin-prediction/results/chignolin_unrelaxed_rank_001_alphafold2_ptm_model_1_seed_000.pdb). The source workspace contains the generated [before/after image](../experiments/chignolin-prediction/chignolin-before-after.png).

See also: [AlphaFold protein structure paper (2021)](AlphaFold-Protein-Structure-2021), [AlphaFold architecture](AlphaFold-Architecture), [AlphaFold evaluation and confidence](AlphaFold-Evaluation-and-Confidence), [AlphaFold limitations and inference](AlphaFold-Limitations-and-Inference).
